issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must confirm it has domestic-relations jurisdiction over divorce, custody, support, and property matters.

issues.label: Personal jurisdiction over parties
issues.why: The court must ensure it has jurisdiction over April and Robert to enter enforceable in personam orders.

issues.label: Venue propriety
issues.why: The court must ensure the action proceeds in the proper county and division under applicable venue rules.

issues.label: Proper service and notice
issues.why: All parties must have received constitutionally adequate service and notice for orders affecting rights and obligations.

issues.label: Due process in hearings
issues.why: The court must provide a meaningful opportunity to be heard on remand issues, including whether evidentiary hearings are required.

issues.label: Magistrate procedure compliance
issues.why: Any reliance on magistrate decisions must comply with objection procedures, independent review, and adoption requirements.

issues.label: Scope of remand mandate
issues.why: The court must follow the appellate mandate and limit proceedings to issues remanded while applying the law-of-the-case doctrine.

issues.label: Law-of-the-case constraints
issues.why: Prior appellate rulings bind the trial court on matters decided and limit relitigation of settled issues.

issues.label: Jurisdiction to modify property division
issues.why: The court must determine whether it has authority to alter property division beyond the limited remand instructions.

issues.label: Jurisdiction to modify support orders
issues.why: The court must determine what child-support orders were temporary vs final and what standard governs modification.

issues.label: Final appealable order status
issues.why: The court must enter a single final judgment resolving property and support as required for appellate jurisdiction.

issues.label: Civ.R. 75(F) single judgment
issues.why: Domestic relations property division must be consolidated into one final judgment disposing of all marital property.

issues.label: R.C. 2505.02 finality elements
issues.why: The court must ensure the order affects a substantial right and determines the action or a distinct branch.

issues.label: Incorporation by reference validity
issues.why: If the court incorporates multiple entries by reference, it must still create a clear, complete, enforceable final judgment.

issues.label: Clarity and enforceability of orders
issues.why: Support, property, and repayment terms must be specific enough for CSEA, parties, and enforcement courts to implement.

issues.label: Shared parenting decree effect
issues.why: The court must account for the existing shared parenting plan and determine how it interacts with current support findings.

issues.label: Child support statute version
issues.why: The court must apply the correct version of R.C. Chapter 3119 in effect for the relevant time period(s).

issues.label: R.C. 3119.04 high-income method
issues.why: For combined income above the statutory maximum, the court must set support based on child needs and parents’ standard of living.

issues.label: Use of worksheet on high incomes
issues.why: The court must avoid using the basic schedule worksheet as controlling when R.C. 3119.04 governs.

issues.label: Determine statutory maximum amount
issues.why: The court must identify the applicable maximum combined income figure (old vs updated) to anchor the analysis.

issues.label: R.C. 3119.04(B) findings for less
issues.why: If ordering less than the schedule maximum amount, the court must make express best-interest findings as required.

issues.label: Findings supporting amount selected
issues.why: The court must articulate reasoning connecting evidence of needs and lifestyle to the chosen dollar figure.

issues.label: Child’s needs determination
issues.why: The court must determine the child’s actual and reasonable needs, distinguishing child costs from parental lifestyle preferences.

issues.label: Parents’ standard of living
issues.why: The court must evaluate the standard of living the child would have enjoyed if the marriage continued, considering both parents.

issues.label: Consider both households’ lifestyles
issues.why: The analysis must consider the child’s experience in each parent’s home under shared parenting, not only the residential parent.

issues.label: Income determination for each parent
issues.why: The court must determine the parents’ incomes relevant to R.C. 3119.04 and explain the basis for any estimates.

issues.label: Imputation vs estimation terminology
issues.why: The court must use proper legal concepts if attributing income due to underemployment or credibility issues.

issues.label: Voluntary underemployment analysis
issues.why: If imputing income, the court must analyze whether a parent is voluntarily underemployed and apply statutory factors.

issues.label: Credibility findings on income evidence
issues.why: If rejecting reported income, the court must ground that decision in record-based credibility findings.

issues.label: Admissibility of financial evidence
issues.why: The court must rule on whether proposed financial documents (tax returns, bank records, affidavits) are admissible and reliable.

issues.label: Discovery entitlement on remand
issues.why: The court must decide whether updated discovery is permitted or required given remand scope and due process.

issues.label: Need for evidentiary hearing
issues.why: The court must decide whether affidavits suffice or live testimony is needed to resolve disputed support facts.

issues.label: Private school tuition allocation
issues.why: The court must decide whether tuition is included in support or ordered separately and allocate responsibility equitably.

issues.label: Health insurance and cash medical
issues.why: The court must allocate health insurance, cash medical support, and uninsured/extraordinary medical expenses per statute.

issues.label: Extracurricular and school expenses split
issues.why: The court must set clear percentages and define covered expenses to avoid enforcement disputes.

issues.label: Childcare and nanny expenses
issues.why: The court must determine whether and to what extent nanny/childcare costs are reasonable and attributable to the child.

issues.label: Deviation factors application
issues.why: Even under high-income analysis, the court must consider statutory deviation factors and explain acceptance or rejection.

issues.label: Avoid double counting benefits
issues.why: The court must ensure tuition/insurance paid directly are not also embedded in the monthly support figure.

issues.label: Tax consequences of support structure
issues.why: The court should consider tax impacts and ensure orders comply with federal/state tax rules on support-related payments.

issues.label: Effective date of final support
issues.why: The court must set a legally permissible effective date and resolve any internal inconsistencies in the decree.

issues.label: Retroactivity authority limits
issues.why: The court must determine whether and how far a support order may be made retroactive under Ohio law and case posture.

issues.label: Credits for temporary support paid
issues.why: The court must calculate credits/offsets between temporary and final support to avoid unjust enrichment or arrearage errors.

issues.label: Overpayment determination method
issues.why: The court must ensure CSEA/accounting accurately computes overpayment amounts and the court independently reviews disputes.

issues.label: Repayment remedy legality
issues.why: The court must decide whether repayment by lump sum judgment or future reduction is lawful and equitable.

issues.label: Interest on overpayments or judgments
issues.why: The court must decide whether statutory interest applies to lump-sum judgments or arrearage/overpayment adjustments.

issues.label: Characterize payments as support vs gift
issues.why: The court must classify disputed payments correctly because enforcement, tax, and offset consequences differ.

issues.label: CSEA role and recalculation scope
issues.why: The court must define what CSEA may recalculate and what remains judicially determined under R.C. 3119.04.

issues.label: Contempt/enforcement implications
issues.why: Support and property terms must be framed to permit or preclude contempt and other enforcement actions appropriately.

issues.label: Res judicata on settled issues
issues.why: The court must determine which claims are barred because they were or could have been litigated in prior phases.

issues.label: Property classification marital vs separate
issues.why: The court must correctly classify each asset and debt as marital or separate under R.C. 3105.171.

issues.label: Tracing separate property contributions
issues.why: Separate-property claims (e.g., Robert’s percentages) require tracing and evidentiary support.

issues.label: Valuation date selection
issues.why: The court must apply the proper valuation date (de facto termination vs other) and justify deviations.

issues.label: De facto termination date validity
issues.why: The court must ensure the chosen de facto termination date is supported by evidence and applied consistently.

issues.label: New Albany value at de facto date
issues.why: On remand the court must establish New Albany’s value as of the de facto termination date per mandate.

issues.label: New Albany equity allocation method
issues.why: The court must decide how to equitably allocate market loss/gain and sale outcomes once the correct valuation is set.

issues.label: Reimbursements for sale expenses
issues.why: The court must determine which sale-related costs are reimbursable and per stipulations or equitable considerations.

issues.label: Effect of stipulations
issues.why: The court must enforce valid stipulations (e.g., repair reimbursement, attorney-fee offsets) and interpret their scope.

issues.label: Attorney-fee offset in proceeds
issues.why: The court must correctly apply the $30,000 fee offset against April’s share as ordered and avoid duplicative adjustments.

issues.label: Separate interest in purchase funds
issues.why: The court must apply the 95.04/4.96 purchase-funds characterization accurately to New Albany allocations.

issues.label: Robert’s Vero Beach correction
issues.why: The court must correct the award to reflect the stipulated marital interest, not the full property value, per mandate.

issues.label: Limit property reconsideration scope
issues.why: The court must not reopen the entire property division when appellate reversal was discrete and limited.

issues.label: Debt allocation corrections
issues.why: The court must adjust jet debt, tax payment, and account withdrawal allocations to 50/50 as ordered on remand.

issues.label: Character of jet services debt
issues.why: The court must determine whether jet charges were marital and allocate them equitably consistent with evidence and mandate.

issues.label: April 2013 tax liability treatment
issues.why: The court must classify and allocate tax debts/payments correctly as marital or separate and apply the remand correction.

issues.label: Marital account withdrawal allocation
issues.why: The court must treat the $20,459.99 withdrawal consistently as a marital dissipation/advance or shared obligation per mandate.

issues.label: Equal vs equitable distribution
issues.why: The court must ensure property division is equitable under R.C. 3105.171, not mechanically equal, and explain deviations.

issues.label: Setoffs between property and support
issues.why: The court must avoid improper commingling of child support issues with property division setoffs absent legal basis.

issues.label: Post-decree property enforcement
issues.why: The court must determine proper mechanisms to enforce property awards (judgments, liens) without altering substantive division.

issues.label: Reduce property award to judgment
issues.why: The court must ensure converting obligations to a lump-sum judgment is procedurally proper and accurately computed.

issues.label: Judgment amount computation accuracy
issues.why: The court must verify arithmetic across proceeds splits, reimbursements, offsets, and corrected allocations.

issues.label: Statutory interest on property judgments
issues.why: The court must decide if and when post-judgment interest accrues on property equalization judgments.

issues.label: Treatment of post-separation expenses
issues.why: The court must decide whether post-separation payments for marital properties are reimbursable or were addressed by temporary orders.

issues.label: Temporary order modification effects
issues.why: The court must account for how the January 2020 temporary support changes interact with final allocations and credits.

issues.label: Mootness of temporary-support motions
issues.why: The court must decide which temporary-support disputes are moot after final orders and which survive for accounting/credits.

issues.label: Contempt and sanctions spillover
issues.why: The court must ensure collateral contempt/sanctions matters do not improperly influence support/property determinations without findings.

issues.label: Restraining order modification authority
issues.why: The court must confirm authority to modify restraining orders affecting accounts and define permissible withdrawals.

issues.label: Custodial accounts ownership and control
issues.why: The court must determine the child’s custodial accounts’ legal status and ensure withdrawals serve the child’s benefit.

issues.label: Dismissal of custodian as party
issues.why: The court must ensure dismissal does not impair the court’s ability to protect the child’s property interests or enforce orders.

issues.label: Best interests of child in finance orders
issues.why: Orders affecting child-related funds and support must comport with the child’s best interests and statutory purposes.

issues.label: Consistency across entries
issues.why: The court must ensure later entries do not conflict with earlier findings/terms, especially regarding effective dates and credits.

issues.label: Authority to reconsider final orders
issues.why: The court must decide whether motions styled as reconsideration are barred and whether relief must proceed under Civ.R. 60(B).

issues.label: Civ.R. 60(B) applicability
issues.why: If relief from judgment is sought, the court must apply the proper standard for vacating or modifying final judgments.

issues.label: Standard of review preservation
issues.why: The court must ensure parties preserved issues (objections, proffers) to permit correct appellate review.

issues.label: Attorney fees already affirmed
issues.why: Because the appellate court affirmed the fee award, the trial court must not revisit it absent permissible post-judgment grounds.
